title: Boss: the till
summary: Four small programs that use everything from this module.

steps.title: Module boss
body: No new ideas here. You have variables, types, arithmetic, strings and input. These four programs make you combine them.
Each one reads input, so check your work against more than one test. Hints are there if you get stuck, but each one costs a little XP.
The last trial is a Sidekick piece, `sk receipt`, and needs three tools for lining text up in columns:
"Tea".PadRight(6) + "|"    // "Tea   |"  (spaces added on the right up to 6 characters)
`"\n"` inside a string starts a new line, so one string can hold a whole receipt.

steps.title: Name tag
prompt: Read a first name and a last name (two lines). Print a name tag: the last name in capitals, a comma, then the first name.
steps.starter: // read two lines, print the name tag
hints: Read the two lines into two `string` variables, in the order they arrive.
`last.ToUpper()` gives the capitals. You can call it inside `{ }` in an interpolated string.

steps.title: Temperature
prompt: Read a temperature in Celsius (it may have a decimal point). Print it in Fahrenheit with exactly one decimal place.
steps.starter: // read Celsius, print Fahrenheit to one decimal place
hints: The input can have a decimal point, so use `double.Parse`, not `int.Parse`.
Multiply by 9 before dividing by 5 and the maths stays in `double`.

steps.title: Change machine
prompt: Read an amount in cents (a whole number). Print how many 50c, 10c and 1c coins make it up, using as few coins as possible.
steps.starter: // read the cents, then work out the coins
hints: Integer division tells you how many whole 50c coins fit: `cents / 50`.
`cents % 50` is what is still owed after the 50c coins. Repeat the idea with 10.
What remains after the 10c coins is the number of 1c coins.

steps.title: The receipt
prompt: Read three lines: an item name, a unit price (decimal), and a quantity (whole number). Print a receipt with 16% tax. All money shows two decimal places.
steps.starter: // read the item, the price and the quantity, then print the receipt
hints: `{value:F2}` prints two decimal places. The total is `subtotal + tax`.

steps.title: Trial 5: Sidekick's day receipt
prompt: **Sidekick piece: `sk receipt`.** Your code becomes the body of
`static string DayReceipt(string name, int tasksDone, int minutesLogged, int goalMinutes)`. The four values are
given (`goalMinutes` is never 0). Put the whole receipt, 8 lines joined with `"\n"` and no newline at the end,
- Line 1: `SIDEKICK DAY RECEIPT` padded on the left to 26 characters.
- Lines 3 to 6 and 8: the label padded on the right to 16, the value padded on the left to 16.
- Times are `<h>h <mm>m` (minutes padded to two digits); the percentage is `minutesLogged * 100 / goalMinutes` in
starter: // name, tasksDone, minutesLogged and goalMinutes are given. Put the receipt in result.
template: static string DayReceipt(string name, int tasksDone, int minutesLogged, int goalMinutes)

Dojo.Eq("Ada's receipt", "      SIDEKICK DAY RECEIPT
--------------------------------
For                          Ada
Tasks done                     3
Time logged               2h 10m
Daily goal                6h 00m
--------------------------------
Goal reached                 36%", DayReceipt("Ada", 3, 130, 360));
Dojo.Eq("title line", "      SIDEKICK DAY RECEIPT", dojoLines[0]);
Dojo.Eq("a long name is right-aligned", "For               Linus Torvalds", dojoLines[2]);
Dojo.Eq("time logged pads minutes", "Time logged               8h 05m", dojoLines[4]);
hints: Work out the pieces first: `string rule = new string('-', 32);`, the two times with `/ 60` and `% 60:00`, and the percentage.
Each middle line looks like `"Tasks done".PadRight(16) + tasksDone.ToString().PadLeft(16)`.
Glue the 8 lines together with `+ "\n" +` between them, and none after the last one.

build.title: The day receipt
build.unlocks: `sk receipt` prints your day, lined up like a till receipt.
transform: // The day receipt: your own passing code from the code-dojo C# track (First steps > Boss: the till).
static string DayReceipt(string name, int tasksDone, int minutesLogged, int goalMinutes)
